text: He quickly prepared a new fire in the open, but his fingers were so numb that he could hardly hold the matches. <break time="0.8s" /> At last he held the whole bunch between the heels of his hands and lit all seventy matches at once. <break time="0.8s" /> He held the blaze to the birch bark, and it was only the smell, not any pain, that told him his hands were burning. <break time="0.8s" /> But a piece of green moss fell on the tiny flame, and when he tried to push it away, the fire scattered and died. <break time="0.8s" /> Then a desperate idea came to him, to kill the dog and warm his hands inside its body until the feeling returned. <break time="0.8s" /> He called the dog, but it heard a strange note of fear in his voice and would not come near him. <break time="0.8s" /> When it finally came close, he caught it in his arms, but his hands could neither hold a knife nor grip the dog. <break time="0.8s" /> Then fear took hold of him, and he ran blindly up the creek toward the camp, with the dog running at his heels. <break time="0.8s" /> He could not feel his feet strike the ground, and it seemed to him that he was flying above the earth. <break time="0.8s" /> Perhaps, he thought, if he ran far enough, he would reach the camp, and the boys would take care of him.
